comments: Fix is waiting in #12573.

Thank you for incredible fast reaction. I've not tested your potential fix yet, but I'd like to point to an aspect that is not covered in the thread/issues you have linked above. Take a look on following part of the log:

Mai 27 18:39:35 xenhost systemd-networkd[21412]: DHCP CLIENT (0x8aa58d0c): lease expires in 59min 57s
Mai 27 18:39:35 xenhost systemd-networkd[21412]: DHCP CLIENT (0x8aa58d0c): T2 expires in 50min 34s
Mai 27 18:39:35 xenhost systemd-networkd[21412]: DHCP CLIENT (0x8aa58d0c): T1 expires in 28min 4s
Mai 27 18:39:35 xenhost systemd-networkd[21412]: lanbond: DHCP lease lost

All timers shows a lot of time until the expiration. Nevertheless it considers the lease as lost. Why? For me it appears to be a core of the problem. Am I wrong?
What do you mean, yuwata, about it?

>On renewal process start address gets immediately removed from the interface. After renewal same address gets reassigned. IPv4 Communication breaks inbetween. Following log illustrates the problem:

What is the guarantee that you will get the same address ? What if your client not able to connect to the DHCP server after lease expired. Are you going to use the expired addresses ? 

To retain addresses use ```CriticalConnection=```.

@ssahani: you are totaly right in case of lease expiration. But in my case lease should not expire yet. T1 timer shows 28min until expiration! It's clear that renewal process starts at ca. 50% of expiration time to have enough time for renewal if first try fails. But the start of renewal process absolutely doesn't meat that the address isn't valid anymore, there is no reason to remove it.
The client may initiate lease renewal prior to T1 timer expiration if it desires.
@ssahani: agree, but if client desires to renew before expiration there is no reason to immediately remove still valid old address leaving the link unconfigured, isn't it?

yeah you have a valid case. I agree. We should verify until t2 expires we should not remove the address.  So we should do something like RFC says

If the client receives no reply from the server, it will remain in the RENEWING state, and will regularly retransmit the unicast DHCPREQUEST to the server. During this period of time, the client is still operating normally, from the perspective of its user. If no response from the server is received, eventually the rebinding timer (T2) expires. This will cause the client to transition to the REBINDING state. Recall that by default, the T2 timer is set to 87.5% (7/8ths) of the length of the lease.
But This does not change the behaviour . This can happen after t2 expired too. What you think ?

@ssahani: IMHO you are correct: if lease expires and renew/rebind retries failing, address gets lost and the link becomes "unusable". But first after the expiration. Currenly I've perfectly responsive DHCP server doing the job properly and the client continiously (twice per; hour because DHCP lease time is set to 1 hout) loosing connections…
Thank you for you patience and support!

I may not catch the discussion, but the PR now
- just drop address and routes when no new lease is obtained. This behavior is not changed.
- when new lease is obtained, then assign new address and then remove old one. Previously, we first drop the old one, and assign new one, even if new one is the same as the old one.

I think T1 or T2 are not relevant here, at least to @avakhit's original issue.
Note that in the PR, `networkd` checks whether the new address is equivalent to the old one or not. So, when we obtain the same address, then the foregoing removing process does nothing.

review_comments: Those error messages talk about stuff "received from the DHCP server". It'll be pretty confusing if any of this is emitted when removing a route for the *old* lease. Maybe this should be updated to not log anything (even at debug level), when operating on old lease?

This removes the call to `link_enter_failed()`. On purpose?

When dhpc_lease_lost() is called twice, warning "DHCP lease lost" will be emitted twice, and various state changes will also happen twice. I think this needs to be refactored to avoid this.
What about the call to `link_enter_failed()`, is it removed on purpose?
When this fails, then dhcp_lease_acquired() already failed, and thus `link_enter_failed()` will called.
